PullRequest.Title: sessions: Preserve confetti position when marking as done
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Confetti could start at the top-left corner because archiving removed the button before its position was measured.

- Capture the button’s bounds and owning workbench before starting the archive operation.
- Reuse that snapshot for menu actions and archive suggestions, preserving theme inheritance, success-only animation, and existing confetti/reduced-motion settings.
- Add regressions for detached animation targets, synchronous session-row removal, and archive-nudge disposal.

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- Focused Chromium unit suites: **49 passing** (Animations, SessionActionViewItem, ChatSessionArchiveNudge)
- ESLint on all six changed TypeScript files
- Launched the Code OSS Agents window from the updated worktree

Scenarios.Scenario: Archive or mark one or more sessions as done from a session row or session header toolbar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click handler now captures one button DOMRect and workbench ancestor synchronously, then awaits the existing action runner. The archive action processes the effective selected-session set sequentially; each session may cancel active chats and then invoke its provider. Confetti creation remains after successful completion and is not required for archive progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel active chat requests and persist/archive the session through the owning sessions provider; provider implementations may dispatch to an agent host or update a remote detached worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For N selected sessions, existing behavior performs cancellation for each active chat and one provider archive per session; the UI action serializes sessions and active-chat cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cancellation/provider operations ran with the same cardinality and serialization; only animation geometry was read after success rather than once before starting the action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing awaits determine archive completion and therefore precede the success animation. The new DOMRect read occurs before them but does not change their count, placement, or concurrency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One geometry capture per click, independent of the number of selected sessions. Existing archive work scales with selected sessions and active chats; the action awaits those operations sequentially.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The changed snapshot is synchronous and singular. BaseArchiveSessionAction loops sessions serially, and SessionsManagementService loops active chats serially before one provider archive call per session; the diff does not change concurrency or add fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The geometry snapshot is intentionally not cached beyond the in-flight click. Existing provider/session caches and any chat model load behavior are unchanged; cold unloaded active chats may be loaded for cancellation, while warm models avoid that load through existing service behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that one geometry read moved onto the pre-action click path when animation is configured, including reduced-motion users. High confidence that it is bounded and does not amplify archive boundary calls; low evidence for a material performance outcome.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A getBoundingClientRect can force layout if style/layout is dirty, but this is one read immediately after an explicit click, with no preceding write in this handler, and it does not scale with selected sessions. There is no evidence of meaningful user-visible input delay.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work is a bounded, single geometry lookup needed to preserve position, while the realistically expensive archive boundaries are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Archive a session from the chat input archive nudge
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The nudge now captures one button DOMRect before setting its busy UI and awaiting onArchive. The callback archives exactly one session through SessionsManagementService; only successful completion with confetti enabled and motion allowed creates the animation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel any active requests and archive the session via its provider; remote providers can update detached worktree/archive state across their existing service boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one archive is in flight from this widget; one provider archive plus cancellation for each active chat in the session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same onArchive callback and provider work were awaited; animation geometry was queried only afterward when confetti actually ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing boundary must complete before success confetti. The new geometry read precedes it but does not introduce, duplicate, or parallelize the boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One button and one session per user-triggered nudge archive. The cost does not grow with transcript length, session-list size, or archive history; existing cancellation work grows only with active chats in that one session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The archiving guard permits one in-flight archive. Existing active-chat cancellation and provider archive work is serialized; the diff adds no queue, burst, or parallel boundary operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is introduced or defeated. Session/provider caches and cold chat-model loading for cancellation are unchanged; the captured rect lives only for the in-flight archive promise.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the before/after placement and one-per-click cardinality; low confidence that this bounded read produces any observable degradation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The new geometry read also happens when confetti is disabled or reduced motion is enabled, but it is one explicit-action read with no local write-before-read pattern. A material layout stall is not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Checking animation eligibility before capture could avoid minor work, but the evidence does not meet the threshold for a concrete performance bug.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mark a chat response as helpful with a configured click animation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The generic MenuEntryActionViewItem now snapshots the helpful button before running the existing synchronous vote action, then starts the configured animation after action completion. The geometry read is on the click path but remains one per vote.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target element and one snapshot per helpful click; no per-message or transcript-wide loop is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The action and snapshot are single-shot. No new asynchronous fan-out, limiter interaction, or concurrent animation burst is introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Animation settings are read through the existing configuration service. No positive/negative cache behavior changes, and the snapshot is discarded after the click handler completes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the generic path now reads geometry before the action; insufficient evidence that layout is invalidated or that this causes measurable latency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A large chat transcript can make a forced layout expensive in principle, but the click necessarily targets an already laid-out footer and this handler performs no preceding DOM mutation. The diff does not establish a dirty-layout trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work is constant per explicit feedback click and no scaling or expensive boundary amplification is present.

Scenarios.Scenario: Trigger confetti, floating-icons, pulse-wave, or radiant-lines animations directly on a live element
Scenarios.CriticalPath: createOverlay now delegates the same geometry and container lookup to captureAnimationTarget. For floating-icons and pulse-wave animations, the changed code reuses that DOMRect instead of issuing the prior second getBoundingClientRect after overlay insertion.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target lookup per animation. Particle and DOM-node counts remain fixed by animation type (for example 24 confetti particles) and cleanup timers remain bounded at roughly two to three seconds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each trigger creates the same fixed animation set as before. The diff neither coalesces nor increases trigger frequency; concurrency remains caller-controlled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cross-trigger cache exists or is needed. The rect is reused only within one animation invocation, avoiding a duplicate live geometry read for two animation types.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that direct-call behavior is equivalent or slightly cheaper and that overlay cleanup remains bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual savings from removing the duplicate geometry read depend on browser layout state; there is no evidenced shipped symptom sufficient to classify this PR as a regression fix.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The helper refactor preserves fixed allocation/lifecycle behavior and removes a repeated rect query for two animation variants.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and every diff hunk. Traced session archive, archive-nudge, helpful-vote, and direct animation paths, including archive provider boundaries, cardinality, cache state, concurrency, layout reads, retained DOM references, and overlay cleanup. The only new pre-action work is one bounded geometry snapshot per explicit click; it does not scale with selected sessions or add/duplicate expensive boundaries, so no high-confidence actionable performance finding was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
